subject: Demo follow-up: model shortlist, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@brightedge.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightedge.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up and asks

Thanks for the walkthrough today — Tim and I appreciated the clear latency and cost comparisons. Two quick clarifications from our side to help with internal prioritization: 

- Primary use cases: query understanding + rerank for search (short contexts, often under 256 tokens) and on-demand paragraph summarization for content editors (up to ~1,200 tokens).
- Latency SLO: p99 under 200ms for the rerank path; p50/p95 for summarization is less strict but we'd like to keep p95 < 1.2s.
- Cost sensitivity: MSP target to keep inference spend below $X/month — we'll share precise budget after internal check, but cost/cost-per-1M tokens is a big factor.
- Security/compliance: data residency must be EU for production; we may run a Private deployment if needed.

Can you send a short recommended shortlist (2–3 variants) with concrete tradeoffs (cost, p50/p95/p99 latency numbers from your benchmarks, and a suggested rollout plan)? Also please include the prompt set and benchmark links you used so we can validate quality internally.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product, BrightEdge AI

[Attachment: brightedge_meeting_notes_20260816.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@brightedge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up and asks

Elena — thanks again for the time. Below is a concise recommended shortlist and rationale based on the rerank + summarization mix you described. I attached the raw benchmark CSV and the exact prompt set we ran (brightedge_promptset_v1.txt) plus a draft mutual action plan.

Recommended shortlist (prioritized):

1) Redwood-13B-ptq (balanced) — recommended start
   - Rationale: Best balance of quality vs cost for mixed workloads. Strong for reranking with tuned prompt templates and for summarization at your target lengths after light prompt engineering.
   - Benchmarks (your prompt set, local emulation): cost ~ $420 / 1M tokens; p50 45ms (rerank), p95 130ms, p99 230ms (single-token decode measured on g4-equivalent); summarization p50 ~ 320ms, p95 ~ 680ms.
   - Notes: Meets p95 summarization goal and is close on p99 for rerank. Suggest KV-cache-aware batching for rerank paths.

2) Redwood-3B-q8 (low-cost, fast) — fallback/cost-optimized option
   - Rationale: Much lower cost; good for non-critical summarization, low-risk rerank where quality tolerance is higher. Useful for bulk processing and cold starts.
   - Benchmarks: cost ~ $110 / 1M tokens; p50 18ms (rerank), p95 48ms, p99 95ms; summarization p95 ~ 360ms.
   - Notes: Small degradation on nuanced relevance judgments; recommend a confidence threshold to route uncertain queries to 13B.

3) RW-70B-fp16 (high-quality, higher cost) — for narrow-high-quality flows
   - Rationale: Best-in-class for subtle semantic ranking and long-form summarization quality. Use case: human-in-the-loop editor flows where quality matters more than cost.
   - Benchmarks: cost ~ $1,250 / 1M tokens; p50 210ms, p95 520ms, p99 980ms (higher variance due to long-context attention); summarization p95 ~ 1.1s.
   - Notes: Likely needs Dedicated or Private to meet latency SLOs consistently; recommend canarying and token/sequence-length caps.

Operational suggestions:
- Routing policy: primary = 13B, fallback to 3B for low-confidence responses, overflow to 70B only for editor-approved flows.
- Canary plan: start with 2% traffic on 13B in EU private/dedicated pool, monitor quality regressions against the brightedge_promptset_v1 and your internal search evals for 7 days.
- Monitoring: set up quality checks (precision@k for rerank) and automatic rollback on quality regression > 3% absolute.

Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_BrightEdge_20260816.csv (raw numbers), brightedge_promptset_v1.txt (prompts used), mutual_action_plan_BrightEdge.pdf (proposed timeline + contacts).

Links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-demo-eval
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/BRIGHT-8421

Next steps (proposed):
1) You + Tim review prompt set and confirm three priority eval examples (we can run an expanded eval quickly).
2) We run a focused quality sweep (10–20k examples) and share a regression report.
3) Agree on pilot scope (EU-only, data residency, SLA targets) and draft procurement timeline.

Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk through numbers — CCing Marissa for procurement and Lauren for security/compliance coordination.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_BrightEdge_20260816.csv (CSV, 1.2MB); brightedge_promptset_v1.txt (TXT, 8KB); mutual_action_plan_BrightEdge.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

From: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightedge.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@brightedge.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up and asks

Karthik — this is great and very helpful. Couple quick clarifications from our engineering lead before we lock the shortlist: 
- For rerank, we expect average request size of ~120 tokens with hot-path QPS ~180 (EU region). Can the 13B profile sustain p99 < 200ms at that QPS with batching/auto-scaling?
- For summarization, editors will run ~3k tasks/day initially; how would you recommend cost controls during pilot?

Also looping in our security contact (will share email) — we need standard SOC2 + EU region clarification in writing for the pilot.

Thanks,
Tim
Senior Eng Manager, BrightEdge AI

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightedge.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@brightedge.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up and asks

Tim — quick answers to unblock procurement and capacity planning: 
- The 13B-ptq profile is our baseline in EU Dedicated pools and our internal stress tests indicate it can sustain the QPS you mentioned with autoscaling and batching enabled; p99 depends on sequence-length mix but we include sequence caps and batch prioritization for hot-routes. We'll provide a short capacity runbook.
- Cost controls: recommend token caps per API key + a budget alert threshold; for pilot we suggest a pre-committed monthly buffer and a burst cap to avoid surprises. I'll attach a procurement checklist and a draft SOW after this note.

Marissa
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: procurement_checklist_BrightEdge.pdf (PDF, 65KB)]

Elena
